## Historical audit: S0175

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/fixed_h0/H0/development/commons_118588033/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines. The supplied observations contain no split lines.

| Stage | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Goal | The student was asked to reconstruct an indoor photograph as separate 3D meshes, matching camera and framing without using the image as a texture. The code’s “shipboard sleeping compartment” is the student’s interpretation, not independent identification of the scene (student request, line 1; response, line 3). |
| Scene construction | The executed final program specifies multiple objects: shell, tiered bunks, lockers, benches, chair, pipes, lamps and wall fittings. It positions separate chair legs, arms and back, and bunk rails and brackets; their actual connections and object poses were not geometrically checked. It specifies colors, roughness and a procedural deck bump material, plus a camera, area lights and world lighting (student execute, line 14). These operations do not establish visual fidelity. |
| Initial failures | Step 1 failed because the telephone-top fillet radius exceeded half its smallest dimension; no image resulted (execution_result, line 5). After receiving that traceback, the student reduced the radius, introduced unique member names, moved several objects and changed the camera (request, line 6; response and execute, lines 8–9). Step 2 then failed because the Blender world was `None`; again no image resulted (line 10). |
| Repair and validation | After the second traceback was supplied, the student added conditional world creation and revised the deck material (request, line 11; response and execute, lines 13–14). Step 3 reported `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file, and was selected (execution_result, line 15; select, line 16). The log reports 16 samples despite the program requesting 48; the cause is unresolved. |
| Review and outcome | The next student request supplied both reference and rendered image with zero executions remaining (line 17); the student replied `DONE` (line 19). This is **formal execution/render success**, not independent verification of camera, lighting, material appearance, pose, connections, occlusion or image match. Visual correctness and overall task quality remain unknown. |

**Input and autonomy.** No teacher intervention is visible in this student trajectory: there is no teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption to attribute. The student did receive runner tracebacks and visibly changed the corresponding code. The recorded sessions report zero student tool calls; exploration consisted of authored programs and three runner executions, not an observed independent search (lines 2, 7, 12, 18).

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, runtime error feedback supported successive repairs, but consumed two of three executions before any render was available. The fillet bound and missing-world fix are concrete technical lessons; the particular compartment layout, camera values and object placements are task-specific hypotheses. Neither image’s pixels are supplied to this audit, so the scene interpretation, whether the deck material actually attached, and whether the final render has framing or lighting problems cannot be resolved from names or success status alone.
